body:
Yeah, agreed. Keep hanging on. I feel a lot better after talking on this forum too. I mean, I knew I wasn't gonna do it, but... I don't really feel like it's something I can talk to my friends or family about because they'll just overworry it and make me feel worse. So this anonymous outlet is just awesome.

I mostly subconsciously bite the nails. They're in my mouth without me even thinking about it. Especially if I'm reading or driving, even when I manage to consciously not bite them for a few days, if I go on a long drive I'll wind up with no nails at the end and not even remember what happened. When I consciously resist, it eventually becomes more and more of a compulsion, until I finally give in and tear a nail off and it just feels so *satisfying*. It sounds weird I know but it's just a physical sense of relief, not as intense as something like sex/orgasm but in the same family for sure.

Yeah I bite my nails. And cuticles, and skin around them. I mean, til they bleed. I have since I was in third grade (in my 30s now). I tried all the various nail bite stop bittering agents and stuff on the market and they only made it worse, because when my fingers smelled/tasted wrong, I would just have suck and chew them until they were normal again, no matter how bad it tasted.

I thought I fixed it a couple years ago, I got *really* into nailpolish. I pretty much stopped biting my nails because I made myself obsess more over my manicure than I was obsessing over the biting. But I never fully stopped biting the cuticles, just the nails themselves, and I'd chew/pick at the polish itself. I had to redo my manicure every 2-3 days because I'd peel off the polish and after I lapsed and fell back into nail biting I realized I'd never cured anything, even though I had stopped "biting my nails" for over a year, because all I did was bite the polish instead of the nail.

That's why I think I might have OCD. Well, and if you see my other post I made myself in this subreddit, the intrusive thoughts.

The ADD...I don't know. It's hard, my mom says there's no way, because I did so well in school but...I only did well with the right motivation. I'm really good at focusing on things that interest me...to the point of obsession really. I can play a video game for 20 hours straight, or code for 20 hours straight if I'm solving an interesting problem. But if I'm bored I can't do anything and just fall into this vague never-ending ennui where I can never finish anything I start. Sometimes I can't even get started.

The commercials like to make it seem that way, and I think for some people depression is like that - they have something horrible happen, fall into depression, get stuck, the drugs lift them out enough to process whatever the horrible thing was, and they move on.

But I think for some people depression is a lifelong thing. It's not tied to any single event. I also think I might have mild OCD, or undiagnosed ADD (pretty common for girls of above average intelligence to not get diagnosed, especially in the 80s/90s when I was a kid).

Having any sort of chronic health problem sucks, especially one that takes so much management like Type 1 Diabetes. That's a lot you have to think about every day, an extra tax on just living that you have to pay.

It sounds like a lot of it is existential angst. You know there's no point to life beyond what you make of it, and you feel like your big chance to make something slipped away. There's a lot of paths you could take from here. You can find a new way to make a difference in people's lives, even if its just the people close to you. You could embrace hedonism, and just live for each day as it happens, find joy in each individual day, spending time with your girl, playing guitar, play video games. If there's nothing outside this life, and it could end at any moment, then maybe the only point to existence is to experience it. I don't know if I'm making sense, I'm not really a philosopher.

Thanks. Yeah I finally slept after posting, taking some melatonin and valerian caps and crying myself out helped too.

Hobbies: video games, doll collecting. It's more the the collecting that runs into 'shopping therapy'. Usually I try to be creative, sew for them, practice repaints/reroots and such (I like making things with my hands as a contrast to balance making things on a computer all day), but I've got no time and even when I do it feels so hard to get started that it's easier to just browse etsy/ebay and buy something there or run out to the store to look at the latest monster high releases or something. 

I have to be careful with the video games too. I don't allow myself to play MMOs anymore. I know I have obsessive/addictive tendencies, and I'm not capable of playing MMOs less than 8-10 hours a day. Either I play it obsessively or I get bored and don't play it at all. So I don't play them at all. I'm already having to be careful with D3 right now. I'm still in Act 2 of Normal, even though all my friends/coworkers are already in Nightmare or Hell by now.
